title: Allowance a Slow Appraisal Attracts on a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Batch
content:
The allowance a late appraisal attracts follows the days the appraisal took, counted in calendar days from the day the batch was booked in to the day the appraisal was recorded, and the programme's appraisal days are read against that calendar count. Both days are read from the Northbeam Renew Trade-In agreement itself.

- Where the appraisal was recorded more than twice the programme's appraisal days after the batch was booked in, the late appraisal allowance of 140.00 USD is added.
- Where the appraisal was recorded more than the programme's appraisal days but no more than twice the programme's appraisal days after the batch was booked in, the delayed appraisal allowance of 60.00 USD is added.
- Where the appraisal was recorded within the programme's appraisal days of the batch being booked in, no allowance is added.

**Both sides of the two boundaries.** An appraisal recorded in exactly the programme's appraisal days was recorded within them, so no allowance is added. One recorded a day later is more than them, and the delayed appraisal allowance follows. An appraisal recorded in exactly twice the programme's appraisal days is no more than twice them, so the delayed appraisal allowance still follows; one recorded a day later than that is more than twice them, and the late appraisal allowance follows instead.

**Worked table on hypothetical inputs.** Take a Renew programme allowing the appraisal 14 days, so twice that is 28 days.

| Days the appraisal took | Allowance added |
| --- | --- |
| 14 | nothing |
| 15 | 60.00 USD |
| 28 | 60.00 USD |
| 29 | 140.00 USD |
| 40 | 140.00 USD |
